codeReview.summary: The research-go-tui.md document (681 lines) is a thorough and well-structured API reference for go-tui v0.11.0. All 9 required topics (a)–(i) are covered with dedicated section headings. It includes 13 URL citations (≥5 required), 28 explicit symbol references (≥3 required), and 3 idiomatic code examples of 23, 35, and 39 lines each (≥10 lines required), demonstrating distinct patterns (composition, state/events+channel watchers, manual event loop). The worker verified against the actual go-tui v0.11.0 source in the Go module cache, which gives high confidence in the API accuracy. I found one minor naming inaccuracy (KeyMap described as `[]keyBinding` but actual type is `[]KeyBinding`) and one API name gap in the gap analysis (uses `WithTrapFocus` but actual API is `WithModalTrapFocus`). Neither issue is blocking for an LLM authoring reference.

issues.description: Section (a) KeyMap description says `type KeyMap []keyBinding` but the actual go-tui v0.11.0 source defines `type KeyMap []KeyBinding` (exported type, not unexported). The correct type name is `KeyBinding`, not `keyBinding`. This is a minor inaccuracy that could confuse an LLM author trying to reference the type directly.

Gap analysis table row for 'Drawer / modal for evidence' mentions 'Modal with trapFocus' and 'WithTrapFocus(true)'. The actual go-tui v0.11.0 API uses `WithModalTrapFocus(v bool)` (in modal_options.go), not `WithTrapFocus`. The approach column should reference the correct function name.

Testing section (h) mentions `mock.String()` and `mock.StringTrimmed()` but the actual MockTerminal API has `String() string` returning the full buffer and `StringTrimmed() string` for trimmed output. The testing pattern example on line 629-635 renders to the app but then reads from the mock terminal — however the code doesn't show how the mock terminal is connected to the app for rendering. The `app.Render()` call renders to the app's internal terminal, not necessarily to the separately-created `mock` variable. This example may not compile/run as written, but it serves as a pattern illustration rather than a copy-paste test.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The go-tui.dev documentation site is a single-page application that returns the same marketing content regardless of URL path. All /docs/reference/* and /docs/guides/* paths resolve to the SPA shell. The worker discovered this during research and fell back to the Go module cache source files. This finding is not recorded in .factory/library/ but would save future workers from the same dead end.

While `make check-doc-links` passes (it skips external URLs), these URLs are effectively dead links for a human reader trying to navigate to specific API docs. This is fine for a reference doc but means `make check-doc-links` cannot validate any of the links (it checks markdown link syntax). This is acceptable for this doc type but worth noting as a pattern.
